mainTopic: Why רב lets the buyer keep a stolen field the גזלן later buys back, which cases this applies to, and whether it clashes with the rule that you cannot sell what you do not yet own.
overview: רב ruled that if a גזלן sold a stolen field and later bought it from the real owner, the buyer gets to keep it. Two reasons were given: the גזלן doesn't want to be called a robber, or he wants to keep his reliability. The גמרא tests two cases where these reasons might differ, a buyer who died and a robber who died, and rejects both. It settles on a gift: by the 'reliability' reason the person who received the field keeps it, but by the 'robber' reason he lost nothing and cannot complain. Next it goes through the ways the field might reach the גזלן: selling it on, inheriting it, collecting it for a debt, or receiving it as a gift. Three אמוראים then argue about how long the גזלן still cares about his good name. רמי בר חמא and רב ששת challenge רב's ruling, saying a person cannot sell what he does not yet own. רבא and אביי defend רב: in his case the buyer truly relies on the seller. Finally רבי יוחנן begins to explain why a sale limited to 'today' is valid, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First proposed difference: the buyer has died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its first suggestion. If the לוקח has died, the 'not called a robber' reason no longer applies, but the 'keep his reliability' reason still applies toward the buyer's children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The buyer has died, so nobody is around to call him a robber. But according to the one who says he wants to keep his reliability, he still wants to stay reliable toward the buyer's children too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing its first attempt to show a practical difference between the two reasons for רב's rule. The test case is when the buyer (לוקח) has died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'not called a גזלן' reason seems to depend on the buyer being alive to do the name-calling. The 'reliability' reason is wider: the seller wants to look trustworthy to the buyer's heirs as well. So in this case the first reason would not uphold the sale, but the second reason would.

keyTerms.meaning: It is preferable / pleasing to him
That he should keep his reliability (his trustworthy name)

phrases.english: he has died.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the buyer. This finishes the sentence just before, which follows the 'not called a robber' reason.

phrases.english: And the one who says:
it is preferable for him to maintain his reliability –
with the children too
it is preferable for him to maintain his reliability.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִית לֵיהּ. וּמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proposed answer to 'what is the difference between them,' which began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is a case where the לוקח died: only the 'reliability' reason would still uphold the sale.

steps.title: Rejection: the buyer's children will also call him a robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא knocks down the first suggestion. Even after the לוקח dies, his children will call the seller a גזלן if they lose the field, so the first reason still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, the buyer's children will call him 'robber'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the difference it just proposed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'not called a גזלן' reason does not need the buyer himself to be alive. His heirs would also be angry and call the seller a robber. So both reasons apply in this case, and there is no real difference here.

phrases.english: In the end,
the buyer's children call him 'robber'!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף קָרוּ לֵיהּ בְּנֵי לוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed difference from step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole 'buyer died' case as a point where the two reasons differ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed the name-calling stops when the buyer dies, but his children would do it too.

steps.title: Second proposed difference: the robber has died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again. If the גזלן himself died (and his children bought the field), the 'not called a robber' reason no longer applies, but the 'reliability' reason might still apply even after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is when the robber died. According to the one who says a person doesn't want to be called a robber, he has already died. According to the one who says he wants to keep his reliability, even though he died, he still wants to keep his reliability!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new case to show a difference between the two reasons: the גזלן himself has passed away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead man cannot be insulted, so the 'not called a גזלן' reason seems to fall away. The 'reliability' reason is about a person's good name, which matters to him even after his death. So only the second reason would uphold the sale here.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier idea and offers a new one)

phrases.english: Rather, the difference between them is
where the robber died.
phrases.notes: The case is that the robber's children then bought the field from its real owner.

phrases.english: The one who says it is preferable for a person
that they not call him 'robber',
he has died.
According to the one who says it is preferable for him
to maintain his reliability,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי אַף עַל גַּב דְּמִית –
phrases.english: here too, even though he died –
it is preferable for him to maintain his reliability!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּמִית גַּזְלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 2 knocked down the first case, this offers a new case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is a case where the גזלן died: only the 'reliability' reason would still uphold the sale.

steps.title: Rejection: his children will be called children of a robber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא knocks down the second suggestion too. Even after the גזלן dies, people will call his children 'children of a robber,' so the first reason still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, they will call his children 'children of a robber.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proposed difference, so neither attempt has worked so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a person who has died does not want his children to carry the shame of 'children of a גזלן.' So the 'not called a robber' reason still applies after his death. Again, both reasons lead to the same result.
steps.whatToRemember: Both attempts to find a practical difference between 'not called a גזלן' and 'keeping his reliability' fail. The shame of being called a robber reaches the buyer's heirs and the robber's own children.

phrases.english: In the end,
they call his children: 'children of a robber.'

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף קָרוּ לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'robber died' case from step 3, using the same 'סוף סוף' style as step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole 'robber died' case as a point where the two reasons differ.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed the name-calling ends with his death, but the shame passes on to his children.

steps.title: The real difference: a field given as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the two reasons shows up when the גזלן gave the field as a מתנה instead of selling it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is where he gave the field as a gift. According to the one who says he wants to stand by his reliability, with a gift too he wants to stand by his reliability. According to the one who says he does not want to be called a robber, he can say to the receiver: What did I rob from you?
steps.whatsHappening: After two attempts were knocked down, the גמרא gives a third answer that holds: the two reasons differ when the field was given as a מתנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'reliability' reason still applies to a gift, because he wants people to trust what he gives them. The 'not called a robber' reason does not apply, because the person who got a free gift lost no money and cannot call him a גזלן.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them in practice

steps.whatToRemember: Gift case: by the 'reliability' reason the receiver gets the field back. By the 'not called a robber' reason he does not, since he lost nothing.

phrases.english: Rather, there is a difference between them
where he gave it as a gift.
The one who says
he prefers to stand by his reliability
with a gift too
he prefers to stand by his reliability.
The one who says
he prefers that they not call him "robber"
he can say to him: What did I rob from you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the two rejected suggestions (steps 1 and 3) with a new case that holds up.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is a gift: the reliability reason still applies, and the 'not called a robber' reason does not.

steps.title: Obvious: if he passed the field on, it was not for the buyer
steps.stepSummary: If the גזלן bought the field back and then sold it, left it in a will, or gave it away, clearly he did not get it for the original לוקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he sold it, bequeathed it, or gave it as a gift, he did not want to establish it for the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section that lists different ways the גזלן dealt with the field. It starts with the obvious cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when the גזלן buys the field back, we assume he did it to make the first sale good. If he then hands it to someone else, his actions show he did not mean it for the first לוקח, so that לוקח cannot claim the field.

keyTerms.meaning: He left it as an inheritance, bequeathed it
To establish it before the buyer, to make the sale good for him

phrases.english: It is obvious:
if he sold it, bequeathed it,
phrases.notes: After buying the field back from the real owner, the גזלן gave it to someone other than the first buyer.

phrases.english: or gave it as a gift

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְאוֹקֹמַהּ קַמֵּי לוֹקֵחַ קָא בָּעֵי.
phrases.english: he does not want to establish it before the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא: זַבְּנַהּ, אוֹרְתַהּ, וְיַהֲבַהּ בְּמַתָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the rule exists to which cases it applies to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the גזלן transferred the field to someone else, the original לוקח cannot claim it.

steps.title: An inheritance came by itself
steps.stepSummary: If the field came to the גזלן through ירושה, it does not go to the לוקח, because he made no effort to get it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it fell to him as an inheritance, an inheritance comes by itself, and he did not make an effort to get it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another clear case to its list: the גזלן inherited the field from the real owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the גזלן going out of his way to get the field, which shows he meant it for the לוקח. A ירושה just happens to him, so it shows nothing about his intention.

phrases.english: If it fell to him as an inheritance,
an inheritance comes by itself,
and he did not make an effort after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַלָה לֵיהּ בִּירוּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case to the list started in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field the גזלן inherited does not go to the לוקח, since no effort was made to get it.

steps.title: Collected for a debt: check whether other land was available
steps.stepSummary: If the גזלן took the field as payment for a debt, we check: if other land was available and he chose this one, he wanted it for the לוקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he collected it for his debt, we look: if the owner has other land, and he said 'I want this one,' then he wanted to establish it for the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a case that is not obvious: the גזלן took the field as payment for money the owner owed him. It depends on the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting a debt usually involves no special effort for this field. But if the owner had other land and the גזלן insisted on this field, his choice shows he wanted it so he could give it to the לוקח.

keyTerms.meaning: He collected it as payment for his debt

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole topic depends on what the גזלן's actions show about his intention toward the לוקח.

phrases.english: If he collected it for his debt,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, so read it as 'collected it.'

phrases.english: we look:
if he has other land
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the real owner who owes the debt.

phrases.english: and he said: This one I want,
he wants to establish it before the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְיַהּ בְּחוֹבוֹ חָזֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the obvious cases, brings a case that depends on the circumstances.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the גזלן chose this field for his debt when other land was available, it goes to the לוקח.

steps.title: No other land means he just wanted his money
steps.stepSummary: If the owner had no other land to pay the debt with, the גזלן took this field only to get paid, not for the לוקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, it was just money that he wanted to collect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the debt rule from the last step. If the owner had no other land, the גזלן had no choice, so taking this field shows nothing about helping the לוקח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, choosing this field over other land showed the גזלן wanted it for the לוקח. Here there was no choice at all. So we only see a man collecting his debt, and the field does not go to the לוקח.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if there was no other land)
To be paid back, to collect a debt

phrases.english: And if not,
it is money that he wanted to be paid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא, זוּזֵי הוּא דְּבָעֵי אִפְּרוֹעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the debt-collection rule from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the owner had no other land, the גזלן collected the field only as payment, so it does not go to the לוקח.

steps.title: A gift: is it like inheritance or like buying?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue about a field the owner gave the גזלן as a מתנה. One says it is like ירושה (it just came to him). The other says it is like a sale (he worked to win the owner over).
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner gave the field to the גזלן as a gift, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says a gift is like an inheritance, because it came to him on its own. The other says a gift is like a sale, because if the גזלן had not worked to win the owner over, the owner would not have given it to him. He worked to win him over so that he could keep his word to the לוקח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: the owner gave the field to the גזלן as a מתנה. Two אמוראים argue whether that counts like ירושה (field stays with the גזלן) or like buying (field goes to the לוקח).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said ירושה does not go to the לוקח because the גזלן made no effort. One view says a gift is the same, since it just landed in his hands. The other view says nobody gives a gift for nothing; the גזלן must have worked to win the owner's favor, and he did that to keep his promise to the לוקח, just like buying it.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift is like an inheritance
On its own, with no effort
A gift is like a sale
He won him over, made himself liked by him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sides. 'Like ירושה' means the field stays with the גזלן. 'Like a sale' means the field goes to the לוקח.

phrases.english: If he gave it to him as a gift,
phrases.notes: The owner gave the field to the גזלן.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.
One says: a gift is like an inheritance,
since it comes on its own.
And one says: a gift is like a sale,
because if he had not taken the trouble to win him over,
he would not have given him a gift.
For this reason he took the trouble to win him over,
so that he could stand by his trustworthiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: יַהֲבַהּ נִהֲלֵיהּ בְּמַתָּנָה, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debt case, the גמרא moves to a new way the field could reach the גזלן: a gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreement: one view treats a gift like ירושה (not for the לוקח); the other treats it like a sale (for the לוקח).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the whole question depends on effort: did the גזלן work to get the field? If yes, we assume he did it to keep his word to the לוקח.

steps.title: Until when does he care about his good name?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: up to what point do we assume the גזלן still wants to keep his good name with the לוקח?
steps.simpleTranslation: And until when does he want to stand by his trustworthiness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking a question. It wants to know when the reason 'he wants to keep his good name' stops being true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole idea that the field goes to the לוקח rests on the גזלן caring about his reputation. But at some point the relationship breaks down, and he no longer cares. The גמרא asks where that point is.

keyTerms.meaning: He is happy to, he prefers

phrases.english: And until when
is he happy to stand by his trustworthiness?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד אֵימַת נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּלֵיקוּם בְּהֵמָנוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reason 'to keep his good name' from step 10 and asks for its time limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The point in time after which the גזלן no longer cares about his reputation with the לוקח.

steps.title: רב הונא: until they stand in court
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the גזלן cares about his name only until the לוקח takes him to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: until the time they stand in court.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the first answer. Once the לוקח sues the גזלן in court, the גזלן no longer cares about keeping his word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking someone to court shows you don't trust him. After that, the גזלן has no good name left to protect with this לוקח. So if he gets the field after that, it does not go to the לוקח.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Until the time of standing in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: עַד שְׁעַת הַעֲמָדָה בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cut-off is when the לוקח brings the גזלן to court.

steps.title: חייא בר רב: until the court document arrives
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רב gives a later cut-off: until the court's אדרכתא document reaches the לוקח.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רב said: until the אדרכתא reaches his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer. He says the גזלן still cares even after the court case starts, until the court gives the לוקח an אדרכתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אדרכתא is a court paper that lets the לוקח go find and take the גזלן's property. Even in court the גזלן can still pay up and save his name. Only when the court has to give out this paper is his name truly lost.

keyTerms.meaning: A court document letting the לוקח find and seize the גזלן's property

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rav said:
Until the court authorization reaches his hand.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets belong to the corrected wording, so read the word as מָטְיָא, 'reaches.'

steps.triggerLanguage: חִיָּיא בַּר רַב אָמַר: עַד דְּמָטְיָא אַדְרַכְתָּא לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, later answer to the question of step 11, differing from רב הונא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cut-off is when the לוקח receives the אדרכתא from the court.

steps.title: רב פפא: until the announcement days begin
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the cut-off is when the court begins the days of announcing the sale of the גזלן's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: until the days of announcement begin.
steps.whatsHappening: A third אמורא gives the latest cut-off. The גזלן still cares until the court starts the days of announcing his property for sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the אדרכתא, the court values the גזלן's property and publicly announces it so the לוקח can be paid. רב פפא says even after the paper is issued the גזלן could still save his name. Only once these announcement days begin is it too late.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of public announcement of the property for sale

steps.whatToRemember: Three cut-offs for when the גזלן stops caring about his good name, from earliest to latest: רב הונא (court case), חייא בר רב (אדרכתא arrives), רב פפא (announcement days begin).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Until the days of announcement begin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: עַד דְּמַתְחֲלִן יוֹמֵי אַכְרַזְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, latest answer to the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cut-off is when the court's announcement days for the גזלן's property begin.

steps.title: The buyer's document is worthless
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges רב: the לוקח acquired the field only through a שטר, and that שטר was written when the גזלן owned nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenged it: After all, how does this buyer acquire this land? With this document! But this document is just a broken piece of pottery!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks רב's ruling that the field passes to the לוקח. He says the sale document has no power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A field is acquired through a שטר. When the גזלן wrote this שטר he did not own the field, so he had nothing to transfer. Buying the field later does not bring that old document back to life.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (an attack on a ruling)
A broken piece of pottery; something worthless

steps.confusionAlert: רמי בר חמא is not arguing about the גזלן's good name from the last steps. He is asking a technical question: what tool of acquisition could actually work here?

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama challenged it:
phrases.notes: He is attacking רב's ruling from earlier, that the field the גזלן later buys goes to his buyer.

phrases.english: After all, this buyer,
with what does he acquire this land?
With this document.
But this document is merely a shard of pottery!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the cut-off discussion of Steps 11-14 and goes back to challenge רב's basic ruling itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the גזלן's later purchase passes to the לוקח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only tool of acquisition is the שטר. It was written when the seller owned nothing, so it cannot transfer anything.

steps.title: The buyer's trust makes the גזלן transfer the field
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: רב is talking about a buyer who trusted the גזלן. Out of gratitude, the גזלן decides to transfer the field to him once he gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Let רב's case be where the buyer trusted him. Because of the pleasure he got from the buyer not questioning him and relying on him, the גזלן goes to the trouble of getting the field for him, and makes up his mind to transfer it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב. He says that in רב's case the buyer trusted the גזלן, and that trust is what makes the transfer work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that the old שטר alone does not work. What makes it work is the גזלן's own decision: thankful for the buyer's trust, he fully decides to transfer the field to him after he buys it. So the acquisition rests on the גזלן's firm intent, not on the paper alone.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Let it be a case where the buyer trusts him.
Because of that pleasure
that the buyer did not say anything to him
but relied on him,
the גזלן takes the trouble and gets it for him,
and makes up his mind to transfer it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא תְּהֵא בְּמַאֲמִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רמי בר חמא's challenge by narrowing רב's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a buyer who trusted the seller
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The transfer depends only on the old שטר, which is worthless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The transfer works through the גזלן's firm decision to give the field to a buyer who trusted him.

steps.title: A ברייתא: you cannot sell what you do not yet own
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא: selling a future inheritance or a future catch is meaningless, unless it is limited to today.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: If someone says, 'What I will inherit from my father is sold to you,' or 'What my net will bring up is sold to you,' he has said nothing. If he says, 'What I will inherit from my father today is sold to you,' or 'What my net will bring up today is sold to you,' his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a ברייתא to challenge רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא teaches that selling something you do not own yet does not work. That is exactly the גזלן's situation, so רב's ruling seems to go against the ברייתא. The 'today' cases are listed as cases where the words do take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing; it has no legal effect
His words stand; it takes effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. The challenge to רב comes from the first half, where selling something not yet owned is worthless.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
'What I will inherit from my father is sold to you,'
'What my net will bring up is sold to you,'
he has said nothing.

phrases.aramaic: מַה שֶּׁאִירַשׁ מִן אַבָּא הַיּוֹם מָכוּר לָךְ,
phrases.english: 'What I will inherit from my father today is sold to you,'

phrases.aramaic: מַה שֶּׁתַּעֲלֶה מְצוּדָתִי הַיּוֹם מָכוּר לָךְ –
phrases.english: 'What my net will bring up today is sold to you,'
his words stand!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's defense, a new and stronger challenge to רב comes from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the גזלן's later purchase passes to the לוקח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says selling something not yet owned has no effect. The גזלן sold a field he did not yet own.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא praises the refutation
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says רב ששת's objection is a powerful refutation of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: Here is a great man, and here is a real refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא reacts to רב ששת's objection. He calls it a strong and convincing refutation of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא had challenged רב himself in Step 15, using logic. Now he says רב ששת has given a solid source-based refutation. This adds weight to the objection; it is not a ruling of its own.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's ruling faces two attacks: רמי בר חמא's 'the שטר is worthless,' which רבא answered with the buyer's trust, and רב ששת's ברייתא that you cannot sell what you do not yet own, which רמי בר חמא praises as a strong refutation.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
Here is the great man, and here is the refutation!
phrases.notes: He means רב ששת has given a strong answer against רב's ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא גַּבְרָא וְהָא תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Agrees with and strengthens רב ששת's objection.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רמי בר חמא views רב ששת's ברייתא as a strong refutation of רב's ruling. רבא disputes this in the next step.

steps.title: רבא: a great man, but not a real refutation
steps.stepSummary: רבא respects רב ששת but says the ברייתא does not refute רב, because in רב's case the buyer trusts the seller and in the ברייתא he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I see a great man, but I don't see a refutation. Here the buyer relies on the seller, and there he does not. Here he relies on him, because the seller will go to the trouble of getting the field for him so he won't be called a robber. There the buyer does not rely on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב against רב ששת's ברייתא. He says the two cases are different, so the ברייתא proves nothing about רב's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said selling something you don't own yet is meaningless. רבא answers that this is because the buyer there doesn't really count on getting anything, since an inheritance or a catch is uncertain. In רב's case the גזלן will work hard to get the field so his buyer won't call him a גזלן, so the buyer truly relies on it and the sale can work.

keyTerms.meaning: A man; here meaning a great person (רב ששת)
His mind relies; he truly counts on it

steps.confusionAlert: The two 'הכא' (here) do not mean the same place. The first is רב's case of the גזלן selling a field. The second is the ברייתא's case of a future inheritance or catch.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of סמכא דעתיה, whether the buyer truly relies on getting the item, becomes the key test for this whole debate.

phrases.english: Rava said: A man I see,
phrases.notes: He means: I see that רב ששת is a great man and I respect him.

phrases.english: but a refutation I do not see.
Here, his mind relies,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is רב's case, the buyer of the field from the גזלן.

phrases.english: and here, his mind does not rely.
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the ברייתא's case of a future inheritance or catch.

phrases.english: Here his mind relies,
that he will go, take the trouble, and bring it to him
so that he will not call him a robber.
Here his mind does not rely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: גַּבְרָא קָא חָזֵינָא, וּתְיוּבְתָּא לָא קָא חָזֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רמי בר חמא's statement that רב ששת's ברייתא refutes רב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's rule that you can't sell what you don't own yet applies to רב's case too, so רב is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only deals with a buyer who doesn't rely on the sale. In רב's case the buyer relies on it, so the sale can work.

steps.title: רבי אבא בר זבדא says the refutation is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The question was sent to רבי אבא בר זבדא, who said the refutation is clear and doesn't need further study.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent it before רבי אבא בר זבדא. He said to them: This doesn't need to go inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The debate is brought to another sage, רבי אבא בר זבדא. He sides with the view that רב ששת's ברייתא clearly refutes רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'it doesn't need to go inside' means the answer is obvious and there's no need for the study hall to examine it further. So he holds the refutation is solid, against רבא's distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, into the study hall for real examination

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא.
phrases.english: They sent it before Rabbi Abba bar Zavda.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: זוֹ אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לִפְנִים.
phrases.english: He said to them: This does not need to go inside.
phrases.notes: He means it's so clear that the study hall doesn't need to discuss it, so the refutation stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְחוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another sage's opinion, agreeing with רמי בר חמא that the ברייתא refutes רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת's refutation of רב is clear and needs no further study.

steps.title: רבא: this needs very deep examination
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי אבא בר זבדא and says the matter needs careful study, repeating his distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This needs to go inside, and to the innermost inside. Here he relies, and here he does not rely.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects רבי אבא בר זבדא's claim that the refutation is obvious. He repeats his distinction from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going 'inside and to the innermost inside' means the matter needs very careful thought, not a quick dismissal. רבא's reason is the same as before: the buyer in רב's case relies on getting the field, and the buyer in the ברייתא does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost inside; very deep examination

phrases.english: Rava said: This needs to go inside
and to the innermost inside.
phrases.notes: He means: think about this very carefully, because the refutation isn't as strong as it looks.

phrases.english: Here his mind relies,
and here his mind does not rely.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: זוֹ צְרִיכָה לִפְנִים וְלִפְנַי לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אבא בר זבדא's view and restates רבא's distinction.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the refutation of רב is obvious.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the difference between a buyer who relies on the sale and one who does not.

steps.title: A case in פומבדיתא: רב יוסף says the refutation is obvious
steps.stepSummary: A real case was judged in פומבדיתא and challenged with the ברייתא, and רב יוסף said the challenge is clear.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case in פומבדיתא, and they challenged it. רב יוסף said to them: This doesn't need to go inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The same argument comes up in a real court case in פומבדיתא. רב יוסף takes the side that the ברייתא clearly refutes רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second round of the same debate, this time in a practical case. רב יוסף, like רבי אבא בר זבדא, thinks the challenge is decisive and needs no further discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in Bavel

phrases.english: There was a case in Pumbedita, and they challenged it.
phrases.notes: The ruling followed רב, and people challenged it using the ברייתא from step 17.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב יוֹסֵף: זוֹ אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְפָנִים.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to them: This does not need to go inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא בְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא וְאוֹתְבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same disagreement in a real case, with רב יוסף taking רבי אבא בר זבדא's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף holds the ברייתא clearly refutes a ruling that follows רב.

steps.title: אביי: it needs deep examination
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רב יוסף and uses the same distinction רבא used.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It needs to go inside, and to the innermost inside. Here he relies, here he does not rely.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects his teacher רב יוסף's view. He makes the same point רבא made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as רבא answered רבי אבא בר זבדא, אביי answers רב יוסף. The buyer in רב's case relies on the sale, while the buyer in the ברייתא doesn't, so the ברייתא is no refutation.
steps.whatToRemember: Two pairs of sages argue the same way. One side (רבי אבא בר זבדא, רב יוסף) says the ברייתא clearly refutes רב. The other side (רבא, אביי) says it doesn't, because in רב's case the buyer relies on the sale.

phrases.english: And Abaye said to him:
It needs to go inside, and to the innermost inside,
here his mind relies,
here his mind does not rely.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: צְרִיכָה לִפְנִים וְלִפְנַי לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's view, the same way רבא rejected רבי אבא בר זבדא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the challenge to the פומבדיתא ruling is obvious.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It doesn't account for the buyer's reliance in רב's case.

steps.title: Why do the two parts of the ברייתא differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says the sale is meaningless in the first part but valid when limited to 'today'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about the first part, and what is different about the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the ברייתא itself and asks a question about it. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both parts the seller doesn't own the item yet. So why is selling a future inheritance or catch meaningless, but selling 'what I inherit today' or 'what my net catches today' valid?

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

phrases.english: And what is different about the first part,
and what is different about the last part?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debate about רב and asks about the inner logic of the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the ברייתא allows a sale limited to 'today' but not an open-ended future sale.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the 'today' sale is for the father's honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that selling 'what I inherit from my father today' is allowed out of respect for the father. He then begins to explain the 'net' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: In the last part, 'what I will inherit from my father today' is valid because of his father's honor. 'What my net will bring up today'...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן starts answering the question. He explains the inheritance case, then begins the fishing-net case, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling a future inheritance should be meaningless, but when it is limited to 'today' the father is dying that day. The son is raising money for his father's needs, likely his burial, so חז״ל made the sale valid for the father's honor. This is a special exception, not a change to the basic rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A trap or net for catching animals or fish

steps.confusionAlert: The 'today' sale is valid as a special exception for a specific reason. It does not mean you can normally sell things you don't own yet.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The last part, 'what I will inherit from my father today',
is because of his father's honor.
'What my net will bring up today'...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סֵיפָא ״מַה שֶּׁאִירַשׁ מֵאַבָּא הַיּוֹם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 by giving a special reason for the 'today' cases.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'today' inheritance sale is valid out of respect for the dying father. The reason for the net case follows.
